parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({
  title: ($json.rule_groups || []).includes('suricata')
    ? `[suricata] ${$json.signature} (${$json.source_ip || '?'} -> ${$json.dest_ip || '?'})`
    : `[${$json.agent_name}] ${$json.rule_desc}`,
  description: [
    `Agent: ${$json.agent_name} | Rule ${$json.rule_id} (level ${$json.rule_level})`,
    `Signature: ${$json.signature}`,
    `Source: ${$json.source_ip || 'n/a'} -> Dest: ${$json.dest_ip || 'n/a'}`,
    `User: ${$json.user || 'n/a'} | File: ${$json.file || 'n/a'} | Time: ${$json.timestamp}`,
    `Groups: ${($json.rule_groups || []).join(', ')}`,
    ``,
    `L1 triage is posted as a case comment. Awaiting analyst approval.`
  ].join('\n'),
  severity: 2, tlp: 2, pap: 2,
  tags: ['wazuh', 'automated', `agent:${$json.agent_name}`].concat(($json.rule_groups || []).includes('suricata') || $json.raw?.decoder?.name === 'json' ? ['suricata'] : []),
  status: 'New'
}) }}

options.systemMessage: You are a Level 1 SOC analyst. You triage alerts and never take action. You have no tools and no credentials. A human reviews everything you write. Work only from the evidence given. Where evidence is missing, write unknown rather than guessing. Consider benign explanations before malicious ones. This is a lab: <LAB_LAN_CIDR> is the protected internal segment, <LAB_INFRA_CIDR> holds lab infrastructure including a Kali machine used for authorised testing. Reputation data is evidence, not proof; a safe score does not clear an address. Return ONE json object with these keys and nothing else: verdict (true_positive|false_positive|needs_investigation), confidence (high|medium|low), severity (critical|high|medium|low|informational), alert_class (reconnaissance|exploitation|malware|policy_violation|authentication|data_movement|availability|other), summary (2-3 sentences for a human), reasoning (3-5 sentences including the benign explanation you considered), escalate (true|false), recommended_next_steps (array of 2-4 read-only investigative actions).
